newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican cabbie tackles Bolivia over "$53,000" cash.
newsitem.headline: Mexican cabbie tackles Bolivia over "$53,000" cash.

text.p: A Mexican taxi driver who shot to fame for returning a briefcase stuffed with cash to its owner, found himself cast as a virtual villain on Tuesday after the Bolivian Embassy suggested he had lied about the contents of the case.
But the unabashed cabbie, Manuel Lubian, insisted on national television that the suitcase left in his taxi that he returned to a Bolivian senator, did indeed contain $53,000.
"I am very sure," he told Televisa's nightly news programme.

Just days after sending a letter to Mexico's largest television station commending Lubian for returning the cash, jewels and papers to the senator, the Bolivian Embassy on Tuesday -- evidently embarrassed by the turn of events -- changed its tune.

"The embassy announces that it has communicated with the Senator Walter Zuleta in La Paz, Bolivia, who assured us that the lost suitcase had 'at the most $1,500 U.S. dollars, credit cards, some jewels of my wife and documents.'
"The Bolivian Embassy in Mexico laments that what was initially considered a recognition by the diplomatic mission of the honesty of a Mexican citizen, has been twisted," it said.
Lubian, who said he had no criminal background, turned down a reward from the senator for returning the briefcase because he felt that to do so would have tarnished "the beauty" inside of him.
Curiously, on Tuesday, the U.S. State Department issued a warning regarding Mexico taxis.

"Growing numbers of U.S. Embassy employees and tourists have been assaulted, abducted and robbed after hailing Volkswagen 'Bug' taxis and other cabs crusing the streets of Mexico City," it said. It warned its citizens to take only authorised cabs.
